en.title: Fresh snow in Avoriaz next week: up to 48 cm on the upper slopes (23–29 November 2026)
en.description: Avoriaz snow forecast for 23–29 November 2026: 29 cm at the top (9–48 cm), 17 cm at the base, snowiest day Wednesday 25 November, with neighbours compared.
en.lede: Avoriaz has fresh snow on the way for the week of 23–29 November. At the top, around 2200 m, our forecast adds up to 29 cm, with 9 cm in a low case and 48 cm in a high one; mid-mountain gets 27 cm and the base around 1200 m 17 cm.

p: At the top (around 2200 m) the week totals 29 cm, 9–48 cm across our range. Mid-mountain around 1700 m gets 27 cm (8–47 cm), and the base around 1200 m 17 cm (4–29 cm).

Day by day, the upper mountain picks up most of it on Tuesday 24 (5 cm, up to 11), Wednesday 25 (8 cm, up to 12), Thursday 26 (5 cm, up to 9) and Sunday 29 (5 cm, up to 8). Outside those days expect little more than flurries.

Next week does not start from scratch. From Tuesday 17 to Friday 20 November our forecast gives the top 56 cm (42–70 cm) and the base 2 cm, the bigger fall of the fortnight. By the time the next round arrives, the upper mountain should already carry a real cover.
Half-and-half at the bottom: 17 cm near 1200 m is a fair amount, but well short of the top's 29 cm. Mild spells will turn the lowest runs heavy and sticky.
Avoriaz is the snow-sure heart of the Portes du Soleil; the lower villages around it are often green in November.

sections.h: When and where to ski Avoriaz
p: If you can pick one day, take the one that follows Wednesday 25 November, when 8 cm (up to 12 cm) has landed on the upper mountain.

Go high: depth is safest on the Hauts Forts and Chavanette, home of the Swiss Wall, and the best skiing should be on the north-facing black runs off the Hauts Forts towards Les Prodains. Treat Morzine and Les Prodains in the valley below as the weak point.

sections.h: Is Avoriaz the best bet nearby?
p: At the top, next week, our forecast gives Flaine (22 km away) 27 cm, Chamonix (28 km away) 27 cm and Verbier (37 km away) 24 cm, against 29 cm here.
The differences are small: the storm covers this whole corner of the Alps evenly, so pick on terrain and lifts, not on the snow total.
The range is wide: 9 cm in the low case, 48 cm in the high one. That is normal a week ahead. The timing is more reliable than the total.
A forecast seven to thirteen days out is a trend, not a ticket.

advice: Fresh snow on a young snowpack: read the French avalanche bulletin (BERA) for the massif before any off-piste plan.
Check the resort's own opening date and lift status: snow on the mountain does not mean lifts are running.
Plan around the top's 29 cm, and keep the high case of 48 cm as a bonus.
